q: In Zechariah, on what animal does the coming King ride?
why: Jesus fulfilled this on Palm Sunday.
quote: humble and riding on a donkey, on a colt, the foal of a donkey.

q: In Zechariah, “Not by might nor by power, but by My…”
why: God's work is done His way.
quote: Not by might nor by power, but by My Spirit, says the LORD of Hosts.

q: In Zechariah's vision of Jerusalem, who will fill the streets playing?
why: Peace will return to the city.
quote: And the streets of the city will be filled with boys and girls playing there.

q: In Zechariah, how is the King coming to Zion described?
why: He is also righteous and victorious.
quote: See, your King comes to you, righteous and victorious, humble and riding on a donkey

q: In Zechariah, God asks who has despised the day of what?
quote: For who has despised the day of small things?

q: In Zechariah's vision, who will sit along Jerusalem's streets again?
why: Each with a staff because of age.
quote: Old men and old women will again sit along the streets of Jerusalem

q: In Zechariah, what happens when the Shepherd is struck?
why: Jesus quoted this before His arrest.
quote: Strike the Shepherd, and the sheep will be scattered

q: In Zechariah, to whom was the word “Not by might nor by power” given?
quote: This is the word of the LORD to Zerubbabel

q: Who was the prophet Zechariah's father?
quote: the word of the LORD came to the prophet Zechariah son of Berechiah, the son of Iddo

q: In Zechariah, what will the seven eyes of the LORD rejoice to see in Zerubbabel's hand?
quote: will rejoice when they see the plumb line in the hand of Zerubbabel.
